To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fatigue is a common symptom of cancer, and that fatigue in cancer out-patients is associated with a wide range of symptoms.

the Edinburgh Cancer Centre Fatigue Symptom Index and Profile (ECF-SP) is an easy to administer and score, 9-item questionnaire that can be used to assess clinically relevant fatigue in cancer patients, that it has good psychometric properties (reliability, validity and responsiveness) and that it has been used in several studies to evaluate fatigue in cancer patients.
the prevalence of fatigue in our cancer outpatients was similar to that reported in other studies and that the prevalence of severe fatigue was high.

the study of fatigue in cancer patients.
the study of the relationship between fatigue, depression and anxiety, and the impact of fatigue on the quality of life of cancer patients.
the development and validation of an instrument that will be used to measure clinically relevant fatigue in cancer patients.

we need to be careful in how we use the term "fatigue" in cancer research, because it is a complex and multidimensional experience that is influenced by many factors, including cancer treatment, comorbidities, and psychological and social factors.
